raw:
**Challenges (strongest flaw, then verdict)**

Dead-path group (items 7-16, 23-25, 30): a node with no input outputs zeros, so any edit on an edge fed by a dead node, or feeding a node cut off from the output, has about zero effect. The risk is sign. "Lower" only holds if the edit usually helps, and "higher" only if it usually hurts. Edits to none usually hurt, so those are safe. Conv edits usually help, so those are safe. Skip edits are riskier because replacing a conv with a skip can lose accuracy or gain it.
- Item 12 (edge 2 to skip, cond edge 0 none): the edit's average sign is mixed, so the contrast could go either way. Keep but low confidence.
- Items 7, 8, 11, 15, 30: keep, since conv upgrades are positive on average.
- Items 9, 10, 14, 16: keep. Deleting an edge normally costs accuracy, and the dead-path case costs nothing.
- Items 13, 23: keep. Edge 1 only reaches the output via edge 5.

Self-condition group (the condition says what the edit replaces):
- Item 3 (edge 3 to skip, replacing none): skip may also be good when replacing pool, so the contrast is not guaranteed. Keep, since replacing none adds a path.
- Item 4 (remove a 3x3 conv on edge 3): the flaw is that all removals hurt similarly. Keep, because 3x3 is the most valuable op to lose.
- Items 5, 6, 26, 27, 29 (removing a pool "higher"): the flaw is that pooling is not always weak, and it can help as a parameter-free path. Keep, since losing pool costs less than losing conv or skip.
- Items 17, 18: replacing a skip with a conv may be neutral, because a conv adds capacity. The contrast against replacing none, which gains the most, still favours "lower". Keep.
- Items 19, 20, 22, 28: adding an op where there was none is the largest connectivity gain. Keep.
- Items 21, 2 (new): removing skip or 1x1 on edge 3 costs more than removing a pool. Edge 3 is the direct input-to-output path, so skip is its strongest op.

Replaced items:
- Original 2 (edge 4 conv3x3 given edge 3 conv3x3): parallel convs are often complementary, not substitutes. Replaced.
- Original 21 (edge 4 skip given edge 3 skip): redundancy is unproven. Replaced.
- Original 22 (edge 5 conv3x3 given edge 4 conv3x3): same substitution flaw. Replaced.
- Original 24 (edge 0 conv3x3 given edge 4 none): edge 0 still reaches the output through edges 2 and 5. Replaced.
- Original 25 (edge 5 skip given edge 3 skip): same redundancy flaw. Replaced.
- Item 1 (edge 5 conv3x3 given edge 3 skip): this is the same kind of weak substitution claim. Kept, but it is the most speculative one left.
